title: Évasion Mont Blanc | Linked ski areas | Snow Catchers
description: How Megève, Saint-Gervais, Combloux and La Giettaz share one pass across two separate lift networks, which base reaches which slopes, how much snow falls at the height these villages ski, what the pass costs, and what the area is like for boarders, families, food and evenings.

hero.lead: Évasion Mont Blanc is one pass over the hills west of Mont Blanc, from Megève and Saint-Gervais to Combloux and La Giettaz, which the operator puts at {{f:op_km}} of piste once Les Contamines is counted. On the snow it is two separate networks, and neither climbs high: skiresort.com puts the lifts between {{f:sr_low|n}} and {{f:sr_high}}. Megève grew into a winter resort around the Rothschild family, and in {{f:rothschild}} Noémie de Rothschild opened the Domaine du Mont d'Arbois above the village.

paras: The larger network runs from Megève to Saint-Gervais. Rochebrune and Côte 2000 rise on the south side of Megève, Mont d'Arbois on the east, and from Mont d'Arbois the lifts cross to Le Bettex above Saint-Gervais, to Princesse above Demi-Quartier and over Mont Joux to Saint-Nicolas-de-Véroce. The smaller network, Les Portes du Mont-Blanc, joins Megève's Le Jaillet sector to Combloux and La Giettaz on the north side of the village.

Megève sits between the two, and no lift or piste crosses it from Le Jaillet to Rochebrune or Mont d'Arbois. Guide Ski and the map data agree on this, so moving from one network to the other means the free Meg-Bus or the car. Les Contamines-Hauteluce shares the pass but lies further up its own valley, reached by road.

Inside the Megève network the weak point is the crossing of the village. Rochebrune reaches Mont d'Arbois only by the Chamois gondola and the Rocharbois cable car, and with the Rocharbois closed {{f:cut.rocharbois|w}} of the journeys between sectors can no longer be made by lift. The Princesse gondola and the Mont Joux chair carry the links to Princesse and Saint-Nicolas in the same way. In Les Portes du Mont-Blanc the three sectors meet around the Christomet, and the Christomet chair and the Bonjournal drag each carry the only lift route for {{f:cut.christomet|w}} of them.

paras: Alti-Mag counts {{f:runs_total}} runs on the pass: {{f:runs_green}} green, {{f:runs_blue}} blue, {{f:runs_red}} red and {{f:runs_black}} black. skiresort.com measures {{f:sr_easy}} of the linked piste as easy, {{f:sr_intermediate}} as intermediate and {{f:sr_difficult}} as difficult.

Green and blue reach almost everything in the map data. Within the Megève network the only gap is Saint-Nicolas, where every route back towards Mont d'Arbois and Megève uses a red, and dropping from Mont d'Arbois to Princesse on easy runs costs one more lift ride. In Les Portes du Mont-Blanc every crossing works on green and blue.

The steep ground is in small pockets. Snowcarbon puts the steepest black on the front of Mont Joly, and Côte 2000 above Rochebrune is short and steep. La Giettaz has the largest share of black in the mapped piste, {{f:black.la-giettaz}}, against {{f:black.mont-d-arbois}} on Mont d'Arbois and {{f:black.saint-nicolas}} at Saint-Nicolas.

paras: This is low skiing by Alpine standards. The lifts start between {{f:lo.saint-gervais|n}} and {{f:lo.la-giettaz}}, and most of the lifts top out below 2,000 m; only the Mont Joly and Épaule chairs climb higher, to {{f:hi.mont-d-arbois}} and {{f:hi.saint-nicolas}} in the map data.

The weather model behind the snowfall figures covers the whole area with one grid cell and adjusts it to three heights. At 1,600 m, close to the middle of the skiing here, a typical season between 1991 and 2020 brought about {{f:s1600}} of snow, more than the cells of the Portes du Soleil and Les 3 Vallées at the same height. At 2,100 m the figure is {{f:s2100}}.

The trend is down. At 1,600 m the typical season fell from {{f:s1600_old}} in 1961 to 1990 to {{f:s1600}} in 1991 to 2020, and three of the last five seasons sat in the lowest third of the 76 year record. The lower slopes depend on snowmaking, and the model gives snowfall rather than depth on the ground.

The season runs from a progressive opening on {{f:open_first|dm}} and a full opening on {{f:open_all|dm}} to {{f:close_all|dm}}. Alti-Mag lists Les Portes du Mont-Blanc as closing earlier, on {{f:pdmb_close|dm}}.

pass.h2: Which pass, and where to buy it
paras: One pass covers both networks and Les Contamines. Six days cost {{f:em_6d}} at the ticket office and {{f:em_6d_online}} bought online at least ten days ahead, a saving of {{diff:em_6d,em_6d_online}} for planning early. A day costs {{f:em_1d}}.

For a week based in Combloux or La Giettaz the local Portes du Mont-Blanc pass covers the smaller network for {{f:pdmb_6d}}, {{diff:em_6d,pdmb_6d}} less than the full pass, though the Megève and Saint-Gervais slopes are then a bus ride and a ticket away.

access.h2: Getting there and choosing a base
paras: By the fastest road Geneva airport is {{f:gva_min}} from La Giettaz and {{f:gva_max}} from Saint-Nicolas, Lyon airport {{f:lys_min|n}} to {{f:lys_max}} and Chambéry {{f:cmf_min|n}} to {{f:cmf_max}}. The motorway runs up the Arve valley to Sallanches and Le Fayet, and the villages lie a short climb above it.

Two railway stations serve the area. Sallanches-Combloux-Megève, {{f:sal_min|n}} to {{f:sal_max}} from the villages, has TGV trains from Paris and the Y83 bus on to Combloux, Demi-Quartier and Megève. At Saint-Gervais-le-Fayet the Valléen gondola has climbed from outside the station to Saint-Gervais since December 2024, with Altibus buses to the other resorts. In Megève the free Meg-Bus runs between the centre, Rochebrune, Le Jaillet, Mont d'Arbois and Côte 2000.

Megève, Saint-Gervais and Combloux fall under the Loi Montagne, which from November to March requires winter tyres on all four wheels or snow chains in the car. There are free car parks at the foot of the Princesse gondola and at Le Bettex, which makes the Megève network easy to start from by car.
access.accessNote: Road distances are the fastest route by the OSRM router on OpenStreetMap data, without traffic or snow. Trains and buses: Megève tourist office (April 2026), Snowcarbon and Guide Ski for Megève. Winter equipment rules: Allopneus (October 2026). Parking: Ultimate France and the Saint-Gervais tourist office. 2026/27 bus timetables have not yet been checked.
basesParas: Mont d'Arbois is the natural base. From Megève centre the Chamois gondola lifts straight into the network, and Rochebrune is {{f:b.mont-d-arbois.rochebrune|w}} lift ride away. Princesse and Saint-Gervais sit on the far side of Mont d'Arbois: from Le Bettex a lift top above 2,000 m is {{f:b.saint-gervais.top2000|w}} lift rides away.

Saint-Nicolas and Rochebrune lie at the ends. From Saint-Nicolas, Rochebrune takes {{f:b.saint-nicolas.rochebrune|w}} lift rides, and from Rochebrune, Saint-Nicolas takes {{f:b.rochebrune.saint-nicolas|w}}. Les Portes du Mont-Blanc is small enough that every base reaches the others in a few rides, but none of its lifts climbs above 2,000 m.

chapters.h2: Riding Évasion Mont Blanc on a board
paras: The freestyle sits on Mont Joux, in the middle of the Megève network. Snowcarbon describes the Snowpark Mont Joux at the foot of the Mont Joux chair, with a hip, a big air, tables and rails, as the easiest park to reach from Saint-Gervais, and the Saint-Gervais tourist office lists a boardercross on the same mountain that emails each run as a video. Megève's own park, Waidzai, lies above the village, and Combloux and La Giettaz keep smaller sets of features.

The trees are the strength here. Snowcarbon sends riders into the Mont d'Arbois woods after fresh snow and into the Magic Garden between the Lanchettes and Radaz lifts above Rochebrune, and points intermediates to the powder under the chair above the Altiport. Ultimate France adds the Route Émile Allais, an ungroomed line down to Cassioz, between Praz-sur-Arly and Megève.

The bigger lines need a guide. The back of Mont Joly, reached by the Mont Joly chair, and the north east slopes off Mont d'Arbois and Mont Joux are exposed to avalanches. Haute-Savoie tourism points to a well known freeride sector on Les Portes du Mont-Blanc, and Snowcarbon calls the steeper slopes of La Giettaz a full day out with few other people on them. On piste, Snowcarbon picks the run from L'Épaule down to Saint-Nicolas, and Ultimate France recommends the Épaule traverse above the village.

Drags are common. In the map data {{f:m_drags}} of the {{f:m_main}} main lifts are drags; they make up {{f:drag.mont-d-arbois}} of the main lifts on Mont d'Arbois and {{f:drag.la-giettaz}} at La Giettaz, against none on Le Jaillet. All of the terrain beyond the markers is uncontrolled, so the avalanche bulletin and a local guide come first.

paras: The pass is kind to the young: children under 5 ski free, and a family buying four or more passes of the same length together, with at least two adults and two under 18, takes a tenth off the total. Combloux holds the Famille Plus label for family resorts, as does Les Contamines on the same pass.

Lessons start young. skiresort.com gives the area top marks for families and notes that the ESF runs children's areas at most base stations, among them Rocharbois, Chamois and Petit Rochebrune in Megève and the Kinderland at Le Bettex. The Pioupiou club at La Caboche, reached by the Chamois gondola from the village, takes children from three in a secure snow garden, with meals included in its five day packages.

Megève starts beginners at Petit Rochebrune, where the Lady tow serves the green Coccinelle, and a beginner pass for the gentle lifts of Rochebrune and Mont d'Arbois costs {{f:beginner_1d}} a day. Above Saint-Gervais a gondola from Le Bettex climbs to Les Marmottons, a beginner area with wide, gradual slopes and the Charlotte la Marmotte play area. For gentle terrain beyond that, Combloux has the highest share of green and blue in the map data, {{f:easy.combloux}}, followed by Princesse and Saint-Gervais at {{f:easy.princesse}}, and Princesse adds a free car park at the foot of its gondola.

Off the slopes, Le Palais in Megève has pools, an ice rink and a climbing wall, and Guide Ski lists a sledge run at Princesse when it is open. On the Jaillet slopes the fun zone of L'Ours des Prés keeps younger children busy.

chapters.h2: Eating in Megève and on the mountain
paras: Megève holds {{f:stars_megeve|w}} Michelin stars in the 2026 guide. Flocons de Sel, Emmanuel Renaut's restaurant, has three of them, and La Table de l'Alpaga and Vous one each. Across the network at Saint-Nicolas-de-Véroce, La Table d'Armante won its first star in 2026. Down in the village, Snowcarbon recommends Benjamin for classic bistro cooking and Le Café for seafood, and notes plenty of pizzerias.

On the mountain, Snowcarbon picks two very different huts. Le Radaz, a small timber chalet at the head of the Côte 2000 valley, is known for its écorce de sapin, a small Mont d'Or baked in its wooden box. On the Jaillet side the Refuge du Christomet is praised for its rabbit and its steak tartare.

Leo Trippi's guide adds more huts on the Megève side: the Alpage de Pré Rosset, with two terraces facing Mont Blanc, the Auberge Bonjournal on the ridge between Megève and La Giettaz, whose terrace looks all the way round, and La Petite Fontaine at the foot of the red Fontaine run, known for its fondue. Emmanuel Renaut also runs Le Boitet on the Saint-Gervais side, a rustic offshoot of Flocons de Sel with a long wine list.

Above Saint-Gervais, Snowcarbon sends skiers to the Relais des Communailles, a terrace and grill in the forest at the foot of the Communailles lift with Belgian beers on the list, to Sous les Freddy's below the Bettex-Arbois lift, and to Le Gouet, halfway down towards Saint-Nicolas. In Combloux, Signature occupies a nineteenth century farmhouse facing Mont Blanc.

paras: The loudest afternoon is on the mountain. La Folie Douce opened at the top of Mont Joux, above Saint-Gervais, in {{f:folie_opened}}, and its terrace looks over the slopes of both resorts with live entertainment every afternoon.

Megève itself is more refined than wild. Snowcarbon describes heated terraces along the pedestrian streets for watching the town go by, and Ski Independence points to the rooftop bar of the Soleil d'Or for a drink with a view.

Later on, La Ferme Saint-Amour serves dinner and cocktails with live music and DJs, and Les 5 Rues, open since 1952, is a jazz club with live music and cocktails. Cocoon Club and the Rendez-Vous Club stay open late, Leo Trippi adds Le Bar du Lodge, and the Stelsia casino offers another kind of evening.

Saint-Gervais is quieter but keeps a handful of bars. At the foot of the gondola up to Le Bettex the Oboose Café has live music and DJ sets, Le Nordique mixes cocktails and Les 3 Mousquetons pours local beers and wines. Bar Le Marie Paradis is on the same list, and down at Le Fayet so is the Lovegood Café. The town also has its thermal spa, Les Thermes, in the park at Le Fayet, and Combloux and La Giettaz are quieter still.

fit.intro: How the area suits different kinds of trip, on the evidence gathered so far.

rows.why: One pass over two networks and Les Contamines.
rows.limit: The networks do not meet, so a day crossing between them starts with a bus.

rows.why: Green and blue reach almost every sector, through forest and open pasture.
Mont d'Arbois sits at the centre of the Megève network, a short ride from each side.
rows.limit: The steeper skiing is scattered in small pockets.

rows.why: Beginner areas at Petit Rochebrune and Les Marmottons, and a cheap beginner pass in Megève.
rows.limit: The lowest slopes depend on snowmaking.

rows.why: Children under 5 ski free, a family discount on passes, and Famille Plus in Combloux.
rows.limit: Prices for lessons and childcare vary by village and are best checked when booking.

rows.why: A park and boardercross on Mont Joux, and good trees.
rows.limit: Drags make up {{f:drag.mont-d-arbois}} of the main lifts on Mont d'Arbois.

rows.why: Trees, the back of Mont Joly and the steeper slopes of La Giettaz.
rows.limit: Only {{f:sr_difficult}} of the piste is rated difficult on skiresort.com.

rows.why: The modelled snowfall at 1,600 m beats the Portes du Soleil and Les 3 Vallées cells.
rows.limit: The lifts climb no higher than {{f:sr_high}}, and three of the last five seasons were poor at 1,600 m.

rows.why: TGV to Sallanches, and a gondola from Saint-Gervais station into the resort.
rows.limit: 2026/27 bus timetables have not yet been checked.

rows.why: Les Portes du Mont-Blanc has its own cheaper pass.

rows.limit: Megève's evenings are polished rather than wild.

rows.why: A pedestrian village centre, Le Palais, horse drawn carriages and the thermal spa at Le Fayet.

fit.catches: Height is the main one. The lifts start between {{f:lo.saint-gervais|n}} and {{f:lo.la-giettaz}}, most of them stop below 2,000 m, and three of the last five seasons were poor at 1,600 m in the weather model. The pass also covers more than the skis can reach: the two networks do not meet, and Les Contamines is a drive away.

compare.h2: The other large areas within reach of Geneva
paras: Set against its neighbours, Évasion Mont Blanc is the smallest of the four on skiresort.com's measure, with {{f:sr_km}} of linked piste against {{f:pds_km}} in the Portes du Soleil and {{f:gm_km}} in the Grand Massif, and only the Portes du Soleil tops out lower. Its share of difficult piste, {{f:sr_difficult}}, matches the Grand Massif's.

Its six day pass is the cheapest of the four at {{f:em_6d}}, against {{f:pds_6d}} in the Portes du Soleil and {{f:F000057}} in Les 3 Vallées. Its grid cell has more modelled snow at 1,600 m than the Portes du Soleil and Les 3 Vallées, and less than the Grand Massif.

items.dd: Megève, Saint-Gervais, Saint-Nicolas-de-Véroce, Combloux and La Giettaz, the linked resorts on the Évasion Mont-Blanc pass, split into the eight sectors that a skier meets on the ground. Les Contamines-Hauteluce and Cordon share the pass but are not linked on skis, and sharing the pass is recorded separately from being linked by lift and piste.

A sector counts as linked only when a route of lifts and pistes reaches it in the OpenStreetMap data. Drag lifts run one way and gondolas and cable cars may be ridden down. The near flat Charmots drag between La Giettaz and Le Jaillet keeps its mapped direction, which the elevation model reads the wrong way round. A link is critical when closing one lift on it cuts routes that no other lift replaces. The model has not yet been checked against the official 2026/27 piste map.

Operator and measured figures are both shown and never averaged. The measured figure adds the skiresort.com listings for Megève and Saint-Gervais and for Les Portes du Mont-Blanc. Mapped piste from OpenStreetMap is used only to compare sectors and grades.
The four areas compared use the same source for each row, so a figure can be set against its neighbour.

method.conflicts: Alti-Mag counts {{f:op_lifts114}} lifts on the pass and the Saint-Gervais tourist office {{f:op_lifts110}}, while skiresort.com lists {{f:sr_lifts}} on the linked slopes without Les Contamines and the map data holds {{f:m_main}} main lifts. Alti-Mag gives the height range as {{f:op_low|n}} to {{f:op_high}}, the tourist office tops it at {{f:ot_high}}, and skiresort.com at {{f:sr_high}}. Alti-Mag closes Les Portes du Mont-Blanc on {{f:pdmb_close|dm}} on its domain page and on {{f:giettaz_close|dm}} on its La Giettaz page. The tourist office lists a week pass at {{f:em_week}} beside the six day price of {{f:em_6d}}. This page names each source alongside its figure.
method.sources: Research of 24 October 2026. Size, runs, lifts and passes: Alti-Mag, Guide Ski for Megève, the Saint-Gervais tourist office and Skiinfo. Measured size and grades: skiresort.com for Megève and Saint-Gervais and Les Portes du Mont-Blanc. History: Wikipedia on Megève. Network, bases, routes and lift heights: a graph of {{f:m_lifts}} lifts and {{f:m_sections}} piste sections from OpenStreetMap (© OpenStreetMap contributors, ODbL), with heights from the Copernicus 90 m elevation model via Open-Meteo. Snowfall: ERA5 reanalysis via the Open-Meteo historical weather API (CC BY 4.0). Road distances: OSRM. Facts from operators, measurements, model results and estimates are kept apart in the research files, and conflicting figures are listed above rather than averaged.
